title: Canary rehearsal script and play notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, repeatable rehearsal script for canary and A/B rollouts. The rehearsal is a dry-run of the full release ceremony focused on operational readiness: wiring observability, exercising rollback, practicing communications, and validating gating heuristics before exposing real user traffic.

Who should attend (roles):
- Release lead (product ops) — drives timeline and decisions
- Oncall SRE/serving eng — validates metrics/alerts and runs rollback steps
- Model owner / ML eng — validates outputs and quality signals
- Observability engineer — ensures dashboards/traces work and synthetic probes run
- Customer success (optional for major enterprise releases) — practices comms
- QA/validation — runs smoke/eval prompt sets

High-level rehearsal objectives:
1) Verify monitoring and alert paths trigger at expected thresholds
2) Validate rollback and fallback paths (model variant, region, capacity tier)
3) Confirm stakeholder comms templates and escalation flow
4) Measure baseline SLOs with synthetic traffic and compare to production baselines
5) Exercise traffic slicing and canary slice attachment/detachment
6) Run an A/B traffic mirror to verify telemetry parity (route-level checks)

Preconditions (must be green before rehearsal):
- Canary build pinned and available in registry (image/model artifact exists)
- Synthetic traffic harness ready with canned prompt sets (latency, quality, edge-cases)
- Playbook runbook checked into repo and shared with attendees
- Oncall rotation assigned for rehearsal window
- Communication channels created: #rehearsal-<release> Slack, escalation phone tree
- Feature flag exists to route rehearsal slices (do not use production slices)

Rehearsal timeline (1.5–2 hours recommended):
- 0:00–0:10 Kickoff: goals, roles, explicit success/failure criteria
- 0:10–0:25 Deploy canary to isolated canary pool (no user traffic)
- 0:25–0:40 Run synthetic smoke: correctness + latency probes
- 0:40–0:55 Attach monitoring dashboards and validate metrics ingestion
- 0:55–1:10 Enable limited traffic slice (1% simulated or internal only)
- 1:10–1:25 Run A/B mirror: compare telemetry to control pool
- 1:25–1:40 Trigger rollback scenario (simulated failure) and perform reversion
- 1:40–1:50 Post-mortem recap & actions
- 1:50–2:00 Close: communication templates, signoffs, follow-ups

Checklist: what to validate at each step
- Deployment step:
  * image/model artifact tagged with release id (check digest)
  * rollout policy set (canary size, timeout, health probes)
  * manifest pinned in release branch (link PR)
- Smoke tests:
  * top-10 user flows return expected outputs (QA pass)
  * end-to-end latency <= baseline + allowed delta
  * token cost per request within expected range
- Observability:
  * dashboards render and show canary data (correlation id present)
  * tracing spans include model-version & shard-id
  * logging shows structured fields: request_type, prompt_id, model_variant
  * alert test: fire synthetic alert and confirm pager path
- Traffic slicing:
  * routing rule uses correct selector (region/customer-tier)
  * monitor request distribution across buckets
  * verify rate-limiting and quotas applied properly for canary slice
- A/B mirror checks:
  * sample of mirrored responses stored for later diffs
  * verify mismatch rate (semantic diff metric) computed and within tolerance
  * ensure privacy controls in place for mirrored PII data
- Rollback / fallback:
  * simulate model OOM or latency spike and trigger automatic fallback
  * manual rollback via console or infra CLI works and is documented
  * fallthrough policy correctly attaches older model variant

Failure modes to rehearse explicitly:
- Metrics ingestion backlog (prometheus push delayed)
- KV cache corruption causing output divergence
- Unexpected tokenization/regression in text normalization
- Regional capacity drain causing degraded tail latency
- Misconfigured feature flag causing bigger slice than intended

Signal definitions and thresholds (examples, adapt per release):
- Latency P95: trigger investigation if > baseline + 50ms, guardrail rollback if > baseline + 150ms for 5m
- Error rate (5xx): investigate if > 0.5%, rollback if sustained > 2% over 3m
- Semantic drift (eval metric on sampled prompts): investigate if quality delta > 3% absolute
- Cost per 1k tokens: flag if > expected by 20%

Observation scripts (short snippets for observers):
- "Confirm span propagation": pick a request id, find trace, ensure model_version tag present
- "Compare control vs canary output": run sample prompt id 453 from eval set and diff tokens + scoring
- "Alert test": open alert endpoint, send synthetic alert payload, confirm alert lands in pagers

Communication templates (use during rehearsal to practice):
- Slack: "@oncall FYI: Rehearsal start — attaching canary pool CN-rc-7 for tests. If you see alerts, escalate to @serving-oncall and @release-lead."
- Pager: "Rehearsal: Canary latency spike observed P95 420ms (> threshold). Follow rollback runbook: run `infra rollback --target canary` and confirm control pool stable."
- Post-rehearsal summary (email/Confluence blurb): short bullets: what ran, signals, action items with owners and ETA

Data capture & artifacts to produce during rehearsal:
- Screencast of console steps (deploy, attach slice, rollback)
- A small artifacts bundle: trace dump, sample responses (anonymized), monitoring screenshots, command logs
- Rehearsal checklist filled out and uploaded to release ticket (Jira key in linked_artifacts)

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How much synthetic traffic approximates real tail behavior for LLMs? (notes: vary prompt length + concurrency; also include cold-cache scenarios)
- Do we need a formal approval step for replays that use live user data for mirroring? (privacy/contract concerns)
- Should rehearsals be mandatory for all major model swaps or only for cross-team affecting features?

Action items (next steps):
- [Ava] Draft a short CLI helper `rehearse-run` that wires synthetic traffic and automates the smoke checks (infra PR stub: linked_artifacts[2]) — ETA 2 weeks
- [Ethan] Build a mini-dashboard template in Console for 'rehearsal mode' that toggles synthetic labels — ETA next sprint
- [Nina] Prepare the canonical eval prompt set for rehearsals (include failure mode prompts) — ETA 1 week

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep rehearsals short; the goal is confidence, not exhaustive testing.
- Err on the side of practicing communications — humans are the slowest part of the chain.
- Save a golden copy of the sample responses (anonymized) for quick diffs in future regressions.

References / further reading:
- rollout-handoff-metrics-checklist-wip (console doc)
- fast-fallback-observation-scripts-for-llm-rollouts-wip (ops notes)

If you're running this rehearsal: paste this doc into the release ticket, attach the artifacts to the ticket, and file a short 10-line post-rehearsal status update in Confluence.
